summary.headline: Indus Towers Q2 FY27: EBITDA up 2.5% QoQ to INR46.3bn (54.4% margin); tenancy ratio improved to 1.63 on 7,900 co-location additions.
summary.overview: Revenue rose 1% QoQ to INR85.2bn and core rental revenue rose 1.3% QoQ to INR54.5bn, with YoY growth of 4% and 3.9% respectively. Reported EBITDA grew 2.5% QoQ to INR46.3bn, and the margin expanded 80bps QoQ to 54.4%, though Q2 FY26 included about INR2bn of write-backs (YoY EBITDA growth adjusted for this was 5.2%). Energy margin improved to -3.6% from -4.6% in Q1 and -4.8% a year ago, helped by an 11% YoY drop in diesel consumption. Management highlighted a strong order book, Africa rollouts starting in Zambia and Uganda, and a strong co-location quarter, while declining to give forward tower or Africa numbers.

segments.name: India towers and co-location
segments.commentary: Added about 2,900 macro towers (+5.6% YoY, base ~270,500) and 7,900 co-locations (+5.9% YoY, base ~440,200). Tenancy ratio rose to 1.63 from 1.62; total co-locations including leaner sites about 454,200.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Towers deployed in Zambia and Uganda in late Q2, with revenue started. Nigeria deployment to begin in the current quarter; Airtel is the anchor customer. Management says early capex per tower is within plan but gave no figures yet.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: Diesel consumption down 11% YoY. Solar sites rose by about 3,000 in Q2 to 49,000; installed solar capacity 297 MW from 259 MW in Q1.

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance on tower additions; management pointed to a strong order book for Q3 and beyond across towers and tenancies.
Revenue growth to track tower and tenancy growth; full-quarter revenue from Q2 additions expected to show up in subsequent quarters.
Africa rollouts to ramp up in H2 FY27; metrics to be disclosed in subsequent quarters.
Energy cost initiatives (solar, lithium-ion batteries, diesel optimization) described as structural, with more room to go; management declined to give margin guidance.
New customer onboarding and renewals continue at a minimum 10-year tenure.
capex_capacity: Growth capex rose QoQ while tower additions fell; management attributed this to a ~INR250cr increase in CWIP and to tenancy, 5G upgrade and solar capex that is not captured in tower counts. Growth-to-operational capex mix broadly unchanged vs Q1.
Analyst cited INR20-25 lakh per new tower guidance; management did not dispute it and gave no per-tower capex figure for India upgrades, calling them site-specific.
Solar deployed at about 3,000 sites in Q2, reaching 49,000 solar sites.
Smart meters deployed on about 140,000 sites over three years.
Network uptime improved to 99.97% from 99.955% QoQ.
demand_pricing: Management says 5G usage grew 79% YoY and is 44% of total data consumption (32% a year ago), per TRAI-referenced data; 5G base reached 463mn subscribers after adding 36mn in the quarter.
Industry added about 30,000 5G BTS in Q2, taking the installed base to about 593,000.
Escalation clauses cover most opex inflation; capex rates adjusted per MSA where flexible. Management did not indicate any additional pass-through beyond the escalators.
IBS: company led incremental market share gains in new IBS deployments for two consecutive years; IBS revenue not disclosed, described as very small.

One major customer's rollouts picked up in the quarter; management declined to comment on another customer's debt raise or on the status of an expired tenancy agreement, saying tenancy is still operated with all customers.

qa_highlights.question: Mix of tenancy growth versus growth from a major customer's rollouts, and does 5G drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5G is not a separate category; the quarter had 2,900 towers and 7,900 tenancies, and the tower-to-tenancy mix will depend on order book. Tenancy ratio expected to remain meaningful given the large 1T tower base for second tenants.

qa_highlights.question: Does revenue growth of about 4-5% accelerate given strong co-location additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to predict; revenue follows tower and tenancy growth, with escalations offset by renewal impact. Full-quarter revenue from additions arrives in the following quarter, and Q2 FY26 had a one-off of about 0.8% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Energy cost per tower is down while energy inflation is high; is this structural and what does it mean for margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to solar deployment, AI-driven diesel planning and the shift to lithium-ion batteries, calling these structural. Margin impact is about 1% vs last year's Q2; management preferred to focus on cost rather than margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why does growth capex per tower look far above the INR20-25 lakh guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO pointed to a ~INR250cr CWIP increase; management said tenancies, 5G upgrades and solar also drive growth capex, so dividing by tower count is misleading. Site-specific upgrade costs were not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2,900 tower count a healthy run rate, and why have leaner towers dropped sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward tower guidance, calling 2,900 robust relative to the industry's current deployment pace. Leaner tower volumes depend on customers' network plans, which are shifting toward macro towers.

qa_highlights.question: Capital structure and a 3-year roadmap: should the company use its net cash for buybacks or an InvIT structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Not addressed directly in the call; no roadmap or capital-structure response was given.

qa_highlights.question: Average residual contract period and lease receivables fell QoQ; are new contracts shorter?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said all new onboardings and renewals carry a minimum 10-year tenure, with no shorter contracts signed.

qa_highlights.question: Africa capex per tower versus peers and the gap size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the lower cost to engineering, vendor ecosystem and India experience rather than scale; no quantified difference given, with figures promised after more deployments.

risks_watch: Growth capex rising while tower additions fall; the gap versus per-tower guidance was not reconciled on the call.
Renewal impact and an expired tenancy agreement still under discussion; management gave no update.
Dependence on one major customer's rollouts and on a second customer's funding plans, which management would not comment on.
Africa: capex per tower, tower count and revenue not yet disclosed at scale; Nigeria deployment due this quarter.
Energy margin remains negative at -3.6%; management declined to give margin guidance.
Flood disruption in Northeast, Bihar & Jharkhand and UP East during the quarter; no quantified impact given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book, co-location momentum and energy cost trends, but evasive on forward tower counts, Africa metrics, tenancy renewals, capex per tower and capital structure, repeatedly deferring to later quarters.
key_quotes: Growth during the quarter was driven by continued network expansion from our customers, alongside a pickup in rollouts by a major customer.
I think the annuity remains 10 years, it's not lower than that.
I think capex per tower, to be honest, in our industry doesn't depend on scale advantage.

growth.why: No numerical guidance; management points to a strong order book and tenancy gains (1.62 to 1.63) with Africa ramp-up in H2 FY27 and no metrics, so growth is directionally supported by towers and co-locations (+5.6% and +5.9% YoY) but not quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 80bps QoQ to 54.4% and energy margin improved to -3.6% from -4.6% in Q1, driven by 11% YoY lower diesel use and solar (49,000 sites, 297 MW), but management declined to give margin guidance and the Q2 FY26 base had ~INR2bn write-backs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Africa rollouts in Zambia and Uganda started late Q2, Nigeria begins this quarter, and ramp-up is scheduled for H2 FY27, with a strong order book cited for Q3 and beyond; no tower count disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Towers grew 5.6% YoY (base ~270,500) and co-locations 5.9% YoY (base ~440,200), tenancy ratio rose to 1.63 from 1.62, and management cites a strong order book, though no numerical tower guidance was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Growth capex rose QoQ with a ~INR250cr CWIP increase and 5G, solar and Africa rollouts are under way, but no new capex plan or per-tower figure was announced and the INR20-25 lakh per-tower guide was not disputed or reconciled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to predict revenue acceleration beyond the 4% YoY and 1% QoQ growth, and gave no numerical guidance, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Renewal impact, an expired tenancy agreement still under discussion, dependence on one major customer's rollouts and a second customer's funding plans, plus flood disruption in Northeast, Bihar, Jharkhand and UP East with no quantified impact.

rows.label: Africa ramp-up (Zambia, Uganda, Nigeria for Airtel)
rows.why: Zambia and Uganda towers deployed and revenue started late Q2, Nigeria begins this quarter, with ramp-up scheduled for H2 FY27; no tower count or revenue disclosed yet.

rows.label: Energy cost reduction via solar and lithium-ion batteries
rows.why: Solar sites rose ~3,000 to 49,000 (297 MW from 259 MW), diesel use fell 11% YoY, and management calls these structural with more room to go, though no margin guidance was given.

rows.label: Strong order book for Q3 and beyond
rows.why: Management cites a strong order book across towers and tenancies, and the quarter added 2,900 towers and 7,900 co-locations, but declined to give forward tower numbers.
